def: Running a system on hardware the customer owns or leases and controls, in their own data centre or building, rather than on a provider's cloud.
A network with no connection to any outside network, so data crosses only by a deliberate, controlled transfer.
A requirement that data is stored and processed in a stated country or region.
The question of whose law can compel access to data, which depends on who operates the system and where that operator is based, not only on where the bytes sit.
The controlled crossing through which code, dependencies and model weights enter an isolated zone after hash checks, scanning and human review.
A machine-readable list of every component in a software bundle, with versions and licences, used to check new vulnerabilities against what was installed.
A model-weight file format that stores a length, a JSON header and raw numbers, so that loading it cannot execute code.
A short list of models and versions that a customer has cleared for use on their data, which limits what a project may choose.
A file of versions, configuration, counts and anonymised failure categories, gathered by a command so the customer can inspect it and release it for support.
